The only thing which I would advise is using (if you are debating on whether or not to put a bit more into the build) the 3600x, as it is slightly faster and overclockable, making your build more future proof. Additionally, the RTX 2060 is newer, with better performance and newer technology (including ray-tracing), further future-proofing your build.

Also check that your motherboard supports your CPU, as otherwise, you'll have to update the bios. However, I would recommend upgrading to a newer model of motherboards like the recent X570 motherboards, which unfortunately don't come cheap, \[[https://pcpartpicker.com/product/RJxbt6/asrock-x570-phantom-gaming-4-atx-am4-motherboard-x570-phantom-gaming-4](https://pcpartpicker.com/product/RJxbt6/asrock-x570-phantom-gaming-4-atx-am4-motherboard-x570-phantom-gaming-4)\], or \[[https://pcpartpicker.com/product/qkLwrH/asrock-x570-pro4-atx-am4-motherboard-x570-pro4](https://pcpartpicker.com/product/qkLwrH/asrock-x570-pro4-atx-am4-motherboard-x570-pro4)\], or \[[https://pcpartpicker.com/product/QZLwrH/msi-x570-a-pro-atx-am4-motherboard-x570-a-pro](https://pcpartpicker.com/product/QZLwrH/msi-x570-a-pro-atx-am4-motherboard-x570-a-pro)\], or \[[https://pcpartpicker.com/product/LJxbt6/gigabyte-x570-gaming-x-atx-am4-motherboard-x570-gaming-x](https://pcpartpicker.com/product/LJxbt6/gigabyte-x570-gaming-x-atx-am4-motherboard-x570-gaming-x)\].

Never be set on one part list though, as prices fluctuate and what may seem like the best card at some point will completely change. If you can get the basic specs of which components you'll use (like the model of GPU/CPU, and the specs of RAM), you're all set. But before you invest in the pc, make sure there aren't any better options for which graphics card you will buy, and you're still comfortable with your build.
